invocation.description: Caller sets JACGRID_WORKDIR to a directory containing task.json (Contract B task envelope) and runs `jac run src/embed.jac`. Per docs/luke-sandbox/spec.md §3: on success the entrypoint writes ONLY the output object — {"results": [...]} — to result.json and exits 0; the SANDBOX (not this workload) wraps that with execution metadata into the full Contract B result envelope. On any failure, result.json is NOT written, an error is printed, and the process exits non-zero — the sandbox's own 'runner exits non-zero / bad output -> error' path builds the error envelope from that. Mirrors sandbox/runners/noop.jac's convention (which also writes only its bare output, e.g. {"echo": ...}, never a full envelope).

env.JACGRID_WORKDIR: absolute path to a writable scratch directory

invocation.on_failure: result.json NOT written, stderr has a human-readable message, exit code != 0

model.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
model.precision: float32, cast to Python float before serialization

runtime_versions.fallback_trigger: sentence-transformers import failure, model load failure, or any exception during encode() — the workload always produces contract-shaped `results`, whichever path ran.
runtime_versions.fallback_scheme: deterministic seeded SHA-256 bag-of-words hash, L2-normalized, 384-d (same dimensionality as the primary model so downstream consumers never branch on it)
runtime_versions.visibility: the on-disk result.json (this workload's output-only contract) does NOT carry this tag — only `results`. Which runtime actually ran is printed to stderr ("connection-embedding: ok, runtime=...") for operator/log visibility; the sandbox's own execution.runtime in the wrapped envelope reflects the allowlisted workload id it invoked (connection-embedding@1.0.0), not this internal primary/fallback distinction. Known limitation for this hackathon iteration — flagged in the app's report.

model.description: informational only — this workload always runs its own pinned model/revision

network.description: the workload forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 / TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 and never fetches weights at task time

output_schema.description: The `output` object this workload writes to result.json on success (per docs/luke-sandbox/spec.md §3) — NOT the full Contract B result envelope. The sandbox harness wraps this with task_id/status/execution/error itself; this workload never writes those fields.

on_failure_contract.description: On failure this workload writes NO result.json at all and exits non-zero (stderr carries the reason) — it does not attempt to construct any part of the Contract B envelope. See docs/luke-sandbox/spec.md §3's Failure mapping table for how the sandbox turns that into a result envelope.

resource_requirements.notes: matches docs/architecture.md §5's example task-envelope limits; measured actual usage on the reference fixture (3 items) was ~500MB peak RSS / ~2.6 cpu_seconds on the primary model path on this dev machine.

tolerance.rationale: the pinned model + normalize_embeddings=True is deterministic per-machine, but float32 BLAS reductions can differ in the last few bits across CPU/GPU backends (MPS vs CPU vs different worker hardware); 0.999 cosine similarity comfortably separates 'same embedding, different hardware' from 'wrong embedding'. Exact bit-for-bit equality is NOT the bar.

verification.runtime_mismatch_policy: if a recompute lands on the fallback runtime while the original ran on the primary model (or vice versa), verification MUST fail regardless of similarity score — the two schemes are not expected to agree.

fixtures.description: 3 short bio-style texts. expected_primary was generated once by running this exact entrypoint against the pinned model/revision offline; expected_fallback is independently computed in Python from the same hash formula as _hash_embed and must match exactly (deterministic, no model involved).
job_type outside this workload's allowlist must fail fast with a Contract-B-shaped error result, not raise.
